about: The demos `alpha demo` can launch. Alpha never links these — add or remove an entry here and Alpha needs no recompile. Each demo runs via its cargo `package` in a source checkout, optionally with a bounded list of package `features`, or a prebuilt `bin` path for an installed alpha (bin wins over package if both are set; a relative bin resolves against this file's directory).

demos.name: walkthrough
demos.summary: Onboarding loop: a deterministic reference author -> build -> sign -> load -> run, then a signed local two-body hand-off, narrated.

demos.name: federation
demos.summary: Many Sanctums x Realms over ed25519 TCP (loopback). ALPHA_DURABLE_BESTIARY=1 runs it on the durable Bestiary.

demos.name: distribute
demos.summary: Two Sanctums over ed25519 TCP (loopback): A publishes a creature, B fetch-loads it in bounded GX chunks with one `registry fetch-load` command, then runs it.

demos.name: bestiary-live
demos.summary: A REAL model authors a creature into a durable Bestiary with a verified proof, journal recovery, and store-level signed-entry convergence (opt-in: needs ALPHA_LLM_MODEL; the runner enables its openai feature).

demos.name: dialogue
demos.summary: Two reference agents hold a multi-turn conversation ACROSS a Realm boundary over ed25519 TCP (loopback): an initiator on one Realm speaks to a stateful responder on another through the Omega gateway.

demos.name: cluster
demos.summary: Three real Sanctum processes across both poles (omega serve + two alpha node operators) form a gossip mesh, cross-execute over it, and prove one pre-admitted remote MCP hub can read a chosen operator's live graph. Manual fail-closed shell/HTTP/MCP runbook.
